exposure: Modified minimal invasive form of uterine preserving surgery (segmental resection of anterior uterine wall)
cohort: Eleven pregnant women with anterior placenta previa and suspected to have placenta percreta who underwent cesarean section.
finding: A modified minimal invasive form of uterine preserving surgery for placenta percreta was successful in 9 out of 11 cases, resulted in significant differences in pre-postoperative hemoglobin and hematocrit levels, a correlation between resected segment volume and number of transfusions, and no maternal mortality or other postoperative complications.
mod_finding: The modified fertility-preserving approach was performed during cesarean sections for women with placenta percreta.
